# Lacuna v0.2.0

Lacuna `v0.2.0` completes the robustness and experiment-lineage milestone. It turns a collection of
successful research outputs into inspectable evidence about how many variants were tried, how a
winner was selected, whether multiplicity-adjusted evidence survives, and whether performance is
stable across parameters, perturbations, time, universes, and regimes.

## Highlights

- Append-only SQLite experiment history with immutable retries, corrections, failures, and complete
  selection lineage.
- Canonical, versioned research fingerprints that reject ambiguous or credential-bearing inputs.
- Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, and Benjamini-Yekutieli corrections.
- Parameter grids with isolation, plateau, boundary, neighborhood, failed-point, and sample-reuse
  diagnostics.
- Seeded continuous perturbations with declared distributions, bounds, named constraints, and
  rejection accounting.
- Half-open subperiod and timestamped universe scenarios with sample/composition evidence.
- Point-in-time-safe fixed or trailing quantile regimes, explicitly retrospective alternatives, and
  conditional outcome/concentration evidence.
- A frozen additive `0.2.x` public API contract that retains all `0.1.x` supported calls.

## Compatibility and distribution

This release keeps `AnalysisResult.schema_version == "1"` and adds public modules without removing
the `0.1.x` surface. It is distributed as checksummed GitHub Release artifacts because the `lacuna`
name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. The release workflow builds and smoke-tests CPython
3.11 stable-ABI wheels for Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64, plus a source
distribution and provenance attestations.

The full implementation record is in the [changelog](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.2.0/CHANGELOG.md), and method assumptions are
documented in the robustness, experiment-lineage, multiple-testing, and regime methodology pages.
